t: How to Know When You Need Traction Outsourcing
d: Three signs your business needs outside help, what Traction Outsourcing does about each, and the results you can expect, in person or remotely.
b: In Nigeria, most business owners do not wake up one morning and decide they need a consultant. For most, the need arrives slowly through years of ignored cracks in business processes. A resignation that should have gone smoothly turns into a 3-week crisis. A client disagrees with an invoice and nobody can find the signed agreement. A good month ends with an empty account, and nobody can say where the money went. The CEO handles each problem as it comes, usually late at night, until keeping the business alive becomes a full-time job of its own. At Traction Outsourcing, we meet owners at this point every other week. Some run a hotel in Abuja or a real estate company in Port Harcourt. Others run a business in Nigeria while working full time in Ontario. The details differ, but the warning signs look terribly similar. Let us see three of the most common signs that you need Traction Outsourcing, what we do about each, and what usually changes once our work is done. Sign 1: The Business Slows Down Whenever You Step Away Travel for two weeks and switch off your phone in the evenings, then see what happens. If many Nigerian CEOs try this, approvals will pile up, staff will wait for instructions that may never come on time, and suppliers who should have been paid on Monday will still have no communication by Friday. This usually happens when a business has grown around one person instead of around a system. Every decision passes through the founder because nobody else has the authority, the procedure or the confidence to make it. While owners may see this as commitment, it gradually becomes the ceiling on how big the business can grow. At Traction Outsourcing, our Operations and Strategy team maps how work actually moves through your business, then formulate process documents that help to guide flow of work. We take time to understand your business and set delegated authority, so each manager knows exactly what they can approve without calling you. When our findings show that the gap is in people, our HR and Leadership team recruits managers who can carry responsibility and trains the ones you already have. The result? Your business keeps running at the right pace while you travel, leaving you time to plan for growth and expansion. Sign 2: Contracts and Compliance Are Handled Loosely In 2026, many business deals still close over a handshake or WhatsApp messages. Yes, nothing may go wrong until something does, and then it costs the business time, money and relationships. Imagine a client refuses to pay the balance and there is no signed agreement, or the agreement was loosely written. Imagine a staff member resigns with your client list and proprietary information, and nothing in their contract or company policy said they could not. Our Legal team takes compliance seriously. Both our in-house team and partner firms follow our strict policies that ensure businesses like yours are fully protected. We audit your corporate documents, draft and review your contracts and staff documents, bring company filings up to date and liaise with government agencies. When a dispute arises, we manage resolution through the appropriate channels saving you years of litigation and court processes. The result? Your business becomes renewed and rebranded from inside out. You can continue to carry on business with confidence, knowing full well that your agreements can be enforced. Sign 3: The Business Is Growing Faster Than Its Structure Growth is good news until your sales double and the way the business runs stays the same. Five staff become thirty, yet there is still no organogram or reporting structure. One office quickly becomes three, but when customers walk in, each branch feels like a different company with inconsistent manners and procedures. Revenue rises, yet nobody has the data to show which product or branch actually makes the money, and when. For businesses like this, Traction Outsourcing brings the structure up to the size of the business. Our Operations and Strategy team redraws reporting lines and builds HR systems for payroll, leave and performance that work the same way in every branch. Our Finance team sets up proper bookkeeping, prepares budgets and produces monthly management accounts, or trains whoever is on your team to do so. With You in Person, or From Anywhere in the World Often, we find that a problem in one area spills into other areas of the business. This is why our consultants provide 24/7 advisory, whatever your time zone and wherever you run your business from. Our consultants work on site with clients in Abuja, Lagos, Nasarawa, Kaduna, Ibadan, Enugu, Ogun, Ondo, Cross River, Bayelsa, Delta and Edo. Many clients, however, do not need us in the same location for the whole engagement, or at any point during it. We have worked with dozens of businesses and hundreds of business owners without meeting them in person, from Nigerians in the US, the UK, Canada, Russia and Australia who run businesses back home, to business owners on holiday in Ghana, Rwanda or South Africa. When a CEO or business manager chooses remote support, they receive the same service and the same quality of result as a client we visit physically. t: Your Annual Corporate Retreat, Fully Handled: Applications Now Open
d: Applications are open for December 2026 to January 2027. We plan and run your company retreat end to end, from venue and transport to awards, gifts and a post-retreat report.
b: Every December, offices across Nigeria start to feel different. Targets are closing, appraisals are due, and somewhere in the building someone asks the question everybody has been waiting for: "Where are we going for the retreat this year?" For most staff, the annual retreat is the reward at the end of a long year. It is a few days away from the desk to rest, laugh with colleagues, look back on what worked and plan for the year ahead. For the HR manager or admin officer who has to organise it, the story is often very different. They spend weeks calling hotels, chasing bus companies, haggling with caterers, printing banners and counting gift items, all while closing the year's appraisals and payroll. By the time the team arrives at the venue, the person who planned everything is too tired to enjoy any of it. Traction Outsourcing Limited wants to take that weight off your team. Applications Are Now Open Traction Outsourcing Limited is now accepting applications from companies that want us to plan and run their annual corporate retreat. This season's window runs from December 2026 to January 2027. Because the season is short and good venues fill up quickly around Christmas and the New Year, we can only take on a limited number of companies. A corporate retreat is a planned period, usually two to five days, when a company takes its staff or leadership team away from the normal work environment. The change of setting matters. People think more clearly when they are away from ringing phones and daily pressure, and they talk more openly when they share meals, games and long evenings together. A good retreat mixes four things: rest, reflection on the past year, planning for the new one, and recognition of the people who made the year work. What We Handle for You, From Start to Finish When you work with Traction Outsourcing Limited, you tell us what you want the retreat to achieve, how many people are coming and what your budget looks like. From there, we take care of the operations end to end. Planning and logistics. We arrange how your people get there and back, where they sleep and what they eat. That includes flights or road transport, airport and hotel pickups, room allocation, meals, security and a clear schedule for every day. Your staff receive one simple travel brief, and nobody is left standing at the airport wondering who is coming to pick them up. Location setup. We find and book the venue, then prepare it for your programme. Halls are arranged for sessions, outdoor spaces are set for games and dinners, and sound, lighting, screens and décor are tested before your team arrives. Branding. Your company's identity runs through the whole event. We produce backdrops, banners, roll-up stands, name tags, branded T-shirts and signage in your colours, so the retreat looks and feels like yours. Content management. A retreat without a clear programme quickly turns into an expensive holiday. We design the agenda with you, line up the sessions, brief every facilitator on your goals, prepare workbooks and handouts, and keep a minute-by-minute run sheet so each session starts and ends on time. Award compilation. Recognition is one of the most remembered parts of any retreat. We help you set award categories, run staff nominations and voting where you want them, compile the results, produce the plaques and certificates, and host the award night. Gift boxes. We source, pack and brand gift boxes for staff, guests and speakers. Each box is shaped around your budget and your culture, from local snacks and wellness items to branded notebooks, flasks and keepsakes. Media management. Our media team covers the retreat with photography and video, handles live social media posts if you want them, and delivers an edited photo album and a short recap video after the event. On-site coordination. A Traction Outsourcing team stays with you from the first arrival to the last departure. If a bus is late or a flight is delayed, we handle it quickly and quietly. Post-retreat report. After the retreat, you receive a report with attendance, staff feedback, key decisions and action points from each session. This helps leadership turn the conversations from the retreat into work that actually happens in the new year. How Your Company Benefits Reduced cost. A company that plans its own retreat deals with ten or more vendors separately: hotel, transport, catering, printing, décor, sound, photography, gifts and more. Each quotes its own price, and extras add up quickly. With one coordinator managing all of them, you get negotiated rates, one budget to track and fewer surprise bills at the end. A wide range of trainers. Through our consulting and recruitment work, we have built a network of facilitators across many areas, including leadership, teamwork, sales, customer service, emotional intelligence, financial wellness and staff wellbeing. We match the trainers to the goals you set, so your sessions speak to the real challenges your team faces. Industry leaders and professionals from West and Central Africa. Your team can hear from experienced business leaders, HR practitioners, founders and specialists from Nigeria and neighbouring countries. Advice from someone who has solved a problem in a similar market often lands better than another lecture from a textbook. Your HR team gets to attend. The people who usually carry the planning can finally sit in the sessions, join the games and enjoy the award night like everyone else. A retreat connected to your people goals. Traction Outsourcing Limited is an HR and management consulting firm, and we look at your retreat through that lens. We think about engagement, retention, culture and performance when we shape the programme, so the fun has a purpose behind it. Choose Your Destination You can hold your retreat in any of these Nigerian locations: Lagos, Abuja, Nasarawa, Kaduna, Ibadan, Enugu, Ogun, Ondo, Cross River, Bayelsa, Delta and Edo. Coast and waterside. Lagos, Bayelsa, Delta and Cross River offer beach resorts, riverside venues and creek views. Calabar and the Obudu Mountain Resort in Cross River are among the best-known retreat spots in the country. Hills and nature. Nasarawa, Ondo, Enugu and Kaduna offer cooler air, green hills and quiet resorts for teams that want space to think. City and culture. Abuja, Ibadan, Ogun and Edo combine good hotels and conference halls with history and heritage, from Olumo Rock in Abeokuta to the ancient city of Benin. For companies that want to travel beyond Nigeria, we also offer destinations in Ghana, Cameroon and Togo . Your team can enjoy the coast of Accra and the hills of Aburi, the black sand beaches of Limbe, or the calm seafront of Lomé. How It Works Apply. Book an advisory call to get started. Discovery call. We learn about your company, your goals, your headcount, your preferred dates and your budget. Tailored proposal. We send a retreat plan with location options, a draft programme and a full cost breakdown. Planning and approvals. Once you approve, we handle bookings, branding, speakers, awards and gifts, and update you at agreed checkpoints. The retreat. Your team arrives, and we run everything on the ground. Report. You receive your post-retreat report, photos and recap video. Secure Your Date Now December and January are the busiest months for venues and hotels across the region, so the earlier you apply, the more choice you have on location, dates and rates. If you want your team to end this year well and start the next one with clarity, let Traction Outsourcing Limited handle the retreat. Book an advisory call at tolnigeria.com/book-a-call to apply for a December 2026 or January 2027 slot. You can also see our other classes and retreats on the events page . How many staff can you plan a retreat for? We plan for small leadership teams as well as company-wide groups. Share your headcount on the advisory call, and we will recommend locations and formats that suit your size. Can we pick only some of the services? Yes. Some companies want the full package, while others only need help with logistics, awards or media. Your proposal will reflect only what you choose. Will our staff need visas for Ghana, Cameroon or Togo? Nigerian passport holders can travel to Ghana and Togo with a valid passport under ECOWAS free movement rules. Cameroon requires a visa for Nigerian citizens, and we guide your team through the process as part of planning.

t: Your Manager Is In Love With Your Staff: How To Manage Romantic Relationships In Your Business
d: A manager and a staff member suddenly get close, and a client deal falls apart. Here is why office romances start, what they cost a business, and how to write a policy that protects yours.
b: A manager and a staff member who suddenly get along very well, a client deal that falls apart, and a CEO who senses there is more to the story. Here is how to manage romance at work before it costs your business. The sales manager now stays back late to wait for the admin officer. They also arrive together and seem to laugh a lot just before they enter the office. He said they live close and he drives, so why not. He is just a kind Samaritan and a good team mate. But everyone notices the quick glances and soft smiles. The receptionist told the unofficial staff group members that the sales manager has ordered food for both himself and the admin officer every day for almost 3 weeks. Then one day, the admin officer came to work by herself, visibly angry at something or someone. The sales manager also arrived in his car at a different time. He seemed reserved and distant at a client meeting. The admin officer was expected to work with him to close a current client on a new deal, but for some reason they both refused to speak with each other and the deal was lost. They apologized but, as the CEO, your mind tells you there is more to what has happened. Romance at work is one of the oldest stories in business, and one of the least managed. Many Nigerian business owners handle it the way they handle a leaking roof in the rainy season. They hope it will stop on its own. It rarely does. Why Romance Grows in the Office Most relationships start with time and closeness, and the workplace supplies both. Between early resumption, long meetings and the traffic home, many workers in Lagos and Abuja spend more waking hours with colleagues than with their families. Shared targets, late nights and site visits also mean shared pressure, and shared pressure builds bonds quickly. Love is not the only motive. In a 2025 survey of more than 1,000 American workers by SHRM, 53 percent of people who had been in a workplace romance said love-related reasons were extremely or very important. Another 29 percent pointed to job-related reasons, such as getting ahead at work. In other words, some office relationships are partly about access, protection or promotion. How Common Are Workplace Romances? The largest surveys come from the United States. Nigerian data is scarce, but our work with businesses across the country suggests the pattern here is at least as strong. SHRM's 2025 research found that more than half of American workers have been in a workplace romance at some point. A CareerBuilder survey of more than 7,780 workers found that 38 percent had dated a co-worker, and 18 percent of those had dated their boss. Vault's 2016 survey found that 50 percent of respondents had been in a workplace romance, and 16 percent had dated someone senior to them. Some industries see more of it than others. CareerBuilder measured five industries directly. For other sectors common in Nigeria, we deduced a likely range from the closest measured industry, adjusted for hours, travel and team make-up. Industry Share of Workers Who Have Dated a Colleague Basis Hospitality (hotels, restaurants, lounges) 47% Measured Financial services and banking 45% Measured Transport, logistics and utilities 43% Measured Information technology 40% Measured Health care 38% Measured Real estate and field sales 40% to 45% Deduced from financial services: target pressure, client visits and late closings Professional services (law, audit, consulting) 38% to 42% Deduced from the overall average, raised for long deadline hours Oil and gas, mining and construction 33% to 38% Deduced from transport: long site rotations, but largely male teams lower the odds Treat the deduced figures as a guide for planning, since no survey has measured them directly. Symmetrical and Asymmetrical Relationships A symmetrical relationship is one between peers. Both people sit at about the same level, and neither controls the other's salary, appraisal, leave or promotion. The risks are real but limited to distraction, gossip, and a team that splits into camps when the relationship ends. An asymmetrical relationship is one where one person holds power over the other. A manager and a staff member in their unit, or an owner and an employee, fit this description. These relationships hurt businesses most. Every approval the manager gives now looks like a favour, and colleagues stop raising problems. If the relationship ends badly, the junior person may say they never felt free to refuse, and a romance can become a sexual harassment complaint almost overnight. In SHRM's 2025 research, 68 percent of HR professionals named favouritism as their main concern about workplace romance, and 61 percent named conflicts of interest. Every approval the manager gives now looks like a favour, and colleagues stop raising problems. The Cost of Romantic Relationships in Business In November 2019, McDonald's removed its CEO, Steve Easterbrook, after finding that he had a consensual relationship with an employee, which breached company policy. He left with a package valued at more than $40 million. A later investigation found undisclosed relationships with other employees, and in December 2021, after the company sued, he returned cash and shares worth about $105 million. In 2023, the United States Securities and Exchange Commission also fined him $400,000. Nigeria has its own example. In 2021, Adam Nuru, then managing director of FCMB, went on leave while the bank looked into allegations about his personal conduct that had become public, and more than a thousand petitioners asked the Central Bank of Nigeria to remove him. The bank's board reportedly found no breach of its policies, and he left the role in July 2021 when Yemisi Edun took over. Whatever the facts, a private matter at the top became a public test of the bank's reputation. The one you have in your business may be smaller, but the implication may hit harder than you can imagine. Should You Allow Your Staff To Date Each Other? Traction Outsourcing's general advice is that businesses should not allow romantic relationships in the workplace. Some office relationships end well. CareerBuilder found that 31 percent of people who dated a colleague married that person. The problem is that the couple keeps the benefit while the business carries the risk. A large company can move one partner to another city, but the more than 39 million small businesses in Nigeria, with one office and one sales team, cannot move anyone anywhere. So when the relationship ends, the tension stays in the business. How To Keep Your Business Safe From Relationship Drama Put it in your employee handbook. Your handbook should define what the business treats as a romantic relationship, state which relationships are not allowed, explain how disclosure works and list the consequences of breaking the rule. Every staff member should sign it. Be clear about what the policy is for. Nobody can stop adults from developing feelings for each other, and a good policy does not try to. The job of the policy is to control what happens when those feelings appear, so the business stays fair, protected, and continues to run. Require early disclosure. If your business intends to allow staff to engage in romantic relationships, staff should be required to inform HR, or the manager in charge, if they intend to start a romantic relationship with a colleague. HR can then move one person to a different reporting line, stop both from approving each other's leave, expenses or appraisals, and keep a confidential record. Train your managers and staff. Training should explain the policy, the difference between a relationship and harassment, and how to raise a concern safely. Apply the rule at the top. A policy that excuses the owner or a favourite manager teaches everyone else that the rule is for small people only. The Practical Takeaway Feelings will always find their way into an office. What you control is whether your business has a written answer ready when they do. Traction Outsourcing Limited helps businesses across Nigeria handle these situations with structure. Our workforce outsourcing and HR consulting service places and manages management staff who respect professional boundaries, and writes the policies that guide them. Our employee training teaches staff and managers how those rules work in practice. Where an owner faces a difficult romantic situation with a staff member, our business advisory team gives confidential, practical guidance. Book a call and let us help you protect your business before the next office story starts. Sources SHRM, Love, Ambition, or Both? New SHRM Research Reveals the Motivations Behind Workplace Romance (2025) HR Reporter, Nearly one-third of workers who had office romance married co-worker: Survey (CareerBuilder) KSAT, SEC charges former McDonald's CEO with misleading investors (January 2023) TheCable, FCMB MD goes on leave as bank probes allegation Ripples Nigeria, FCMB appoints Yemisi Edun as MD to succeed Adam Nuru (July 2021) Should employees be allowed to date each other at work? Traction Outsourcing's general advice is that businesses should not allow romantic relationships in the workplace. Even when a relationship ends well, the business carries the risk of favouritism, conflict of interest and tension if it ends badly, and most Nigerian small businesses have no way to move one partner to another office or team. What is the difference between a symmetrical and an asymmetrical workplace relationship? A symmetrical relationship is between peers, where neither person controls the other's pay, appraisal, leave or promotion. An asymmetrical relationship is one where one person holds power over the other, such as a manager and a staff member in their unit. Asymmetrical relationships hurt businesses most because every approval can look like a favour and a break-up can turn into a harassment complaint. What should a workplace romance policy include? Define what the business treats as a romantic relationship, state which relationships are not allowed, explain how disclosure works and list the consequences of breaking the rule. Require early disclosure to HR, move one person to a different reporting line where needed, keep a confidential record, train managers and staff, and apply the rule to the owner and senior managers too. How common are romances between colleagues? SHRM's 2025 research found that more than half of American workers have been in a workplace romance at some point, and a CareerBuilder survey found that 38 percent had dated a co-worker. Nigerian data is scarce, but the pattern is likely at least as strong in industries with long hours, travel and shared targets.

t: Traction Outsourcing HRMS Is Now on the Web: Manage Your Staff From Anywhere, on Any Device
d: Traction Outsourcing HRMS is now a web app. Manage staff, Nigerian payroll, leave and recruitment from any device, wherever you are in the world.
b: Abuja, Nigeria. Traction Outsourcing Limited has launched the web version of Traction Outsourcing HRMS, its human resource management software built for Nigerian businesses. The software was previously available only as a desktop application. It can now be used through any internet browser on a phone, tablet, laptop or desktop computer, at any hour and from any location. Business owners can now check staff records, run payroll, approve leave and follow up on recruitment without needing to sit in front of one office computer. What an HRMS Does An HRMS, short for Human Resource Management System, is software that keeps all the information and activities connected to your staff in one place. That includes each employee's personal file, their salary and deductions, their leave days, their performance reviews, the training they have attended and the candidates you are interviewing for open roles. Without a system like this, most businesses keep staff information in a mix of paper files, Excel sheets, WhatsApp chats and the memory of one HR officer. When that officer resigns or travels, a large part of what the business knows about its own people leaves with them. Why Many Businesses Give Up on HR Software Many Nigerian business owners have tried HR software before and abandoned it within months. In our work with clients in Abuja, Lagos and other cities, the same complaints come up again and again. The first is that much of the software on the market was designed for other countries. This means HR managers and business owners will struggle with Nigerian statutory deductions, legal limits, and other labour law requirements. The second complaint is pricing. Many foreign tools are billed in dollars and business owners cannot accurately budget for it. So, a subscription that looked affordable in January can become a burden by June if the naira weakens. The third is that older systems are tied to one computer in one office. Information is entered at headquarters and stays there. This means that the branch manager in Kano, the business owner on a business trip to Accra, or the HR officer working from home on a public holiday cannot access it. Finally, many tools are built for HR specialists. They come with so many settings and menus that a small business owner or a busy admin officer never find the time to learn them. What We Changed Traction Outsourcing HRMS started as a desktop application, meaning it had to be installed on a particular computer before anyone could use it. This type of application worked for businesses with a single office, but it left out many of the employers who needed it most. The new web version removes that limit. Your records are kept in the cloud, and you can sign in from anywhere in the world, on any device. Built for Owners in the Diaspora A large number of Nigerian businesses are owned by people who live abroad. They put their savings into a pharmacy, a school, a logistics company or a hotel back home, then depend on a manager to run it day to day. For many of them, the hardest part is knowing what is really happening with their staff. How many people resumed this month? Who is on leave? Did the salary schedule sent over last week match the actual headcount? These questions usually end in long phone calls across time zones and a great deal of trust placed in one or two people. With Traction Outsourcing HRMS, a Nigerian business owner in the UK or anywhere else can open the system on their phone and check staff records, payroll and leave for themselves. Built for Businesses With Branches Business owners who run branches in several cities face a similar problem. A restaurant group with outlets in Abuja, Lagos and Port Harcourt, or a school with campuses in three states, often ends up with three different ways of keeping staff records. Each branch has its own spreadsheet, its own way of counting leave and its own way of reporting salaries. Head office hears about problems weeks after they start. Traction Outsourcing HRMS brings every branch into one system. Staff in each location sit under the same company account, follow the same leave and payroll rules, and appear in the same records. The owner or head of HR can see the whole workforce in one place and catch a problem in one city before it spreads to another. Why We Built It Traction Outsourcing Limited has spent years helping Nigerian businesses build their HR structures, from employee handbooks and payroll set-ups to recruitment. Over that time, we have watched good HR policies fail because there was no simple tool to apply them every day. Rules get bent because nobody is counting. Salaries go out wrong because the deduction sheet was last updated two years ago. Records disappear when a staff member leaves. Traction Outsourcing HRMS is our response to these problems and more. It was shaped by the questions business owners and HR managers bring to us every week. Businesses that want support beyond the software can still rely on our team for Business and HR consulting, corporate restructuring, policy writing and workforce management.
